s_param.name: name
s_param.description: Human-readable name for the app (used to tag tools and identify the app). Typical usage: FastMCPApp("Dashboard").

examples.code:
from fastmcp.apps.app import FastMCPApp

# Minimal app with a human-readable name
app = FastMCPApp("Dashboard")
print("App name:", getattr(app, "name", None))
print("App config:", getattr(app, "config", None))

mechanism.text:
Acts as an application-scoped registry and local provider wrapper for tools, UI components, resources and prompts — essentially the owner/manager that declares what an app exposes to a running FastMCP server. An instance holds the app identity (name) and a LocalProvider used as the on-disk / in-process component store; it is responsible for annotating components with app metadata (visibility, app name, and a deterministic tool hash) and registering them into that local store.

Construction is lightweight: you create it with an application name and it instantiates its internal LocalProvider. Typical usage is declarative: call its decorator-like methods (tool, ui) or add_tool to register callables or Tool objects. Those registration helpers resolve names, assemble UI/resource metadata (including visibility and renderer hints), compute addressing hashes, attach auth/timeout/meta, and hand the Tool to the internal provider. The instance itself is not a running server; it provides an async lifespan context that proxies to the LocalProvider’s lifespan for any async setup/teardown the provider requires. To actually serve the app’s tools, the instance is added to a FastMCP server (via run or server.add_provider).

Important lifecycle notes: the LocalProvider lifecycle is managed through the app’s lifespan context manager; for proper resource cleanup any async initialization/teardown should be driven by entering/exiting lifespan. run starts a server process and does not imply additional implicit disposal of the LocalProvider beyond its lifespan — callers should use lifespan when lifecycle control is required.

Key invariants and role in architecture:
- Every registered component will carry fastmcp.app metadata linking it to this app and a stable _tool_hash derived from (app, tool name).
- UI components are given renderer/resource URIs and appropriate visibility; tools default to app-only visibility unless explicitly exposed to model.
- The instance is a coordinator/builder: it doesn’t execute tools itself but prepares, annotates and stores them in a provider that the server will expose.
